title: The Shape of the Arm: Capsules for the Links, Spheres, Boxes and a Floor for the World, and the Pairs of Links That Must Not Be Asked

questions.question: Why are links modelled as capsules?
options: A segment and a radius fit a long link well and cost almost nothing to check
A capsule is the exact shape of a link
Capsules are the only shape with a signed distance
A capsule never overlaps its neighbour at a joint
questions.explanation: A link is a long thing between two joints. One segment and one radius cover it closely, and the distance to a segment is a standard, cheap calculation.

questions.question: The distance of a capsule of radius 0.1 to a sphere of radius 0.2 with centres 1 m apart was:
options: 0.300 m clear
0.700 m clear
1.000 m clear, since the centres are what count
0.800 m clear, the larger radius taken off
questions.explanation: The distance between the segment and the sphere's centre, less both radii: 1 less 0.1 less 0.2.

questions.question: With the floor raised to 0.4 m the arm's signed distance was:
options: 0.140 m, as before
0.000 m: just touching
-0.160 m: negative, through it
0.160 m, clear
questions.explanation: Raising the floor by 0.3 m took the clearance from 0.140 m to 0.160 m below zero. The sign says the arm is through it and the size says how far to push it out.

questions.question: How many pairs of links does the self check ask about, for four capsules?
options: 6, every pair
4, one for each capsule
2, the base against the last two
questions.explanation: Neighbours share a joint and always touch there, so asking about them would always say collision. Of the 6 pairs, the 3 that are more than one apart are asked.

questions.question: Why is a collision model that is a little too big better than one that is a little too small?
options: It is cheaper to compute than an exact one
It keeps the planner a little further away than it needs to; too small hits things
The planner finds shorter paths with larger shapes
A larger model lets the checker take larger steps
questions.explanation: Both are wrong, in different directions. Too big costs a little room; too small lets a path through that the real arm cannot take.

questions.question: Why does a segment to box distance work by a ternary search?
options: A box has too many faces to test one by one
The closed form exists but is slower
The segment may pass through the box
The distance of a point to a convex set is convex along a line: one minimum
questions.explanation: There is no formula, but along the segment the distance to a convex shape has a single low point, and a search that narrows on it cannot be fooled by a second one.
